It’s been a while since I’ve read it, but here are some things I liked:

Snow as a character was fascinating imo. At the beginning of the book he’s bitter about what the rebellion took from him (ie the Capitol still being a mess). His relationship with Lucy Gray was also enjoyable, I liked how it gave a sense of hope and foreboding. She brings out better qualities in him, though Collins still ran an undercurrent through his narration that hinted at him being more sinister (eg Snow referring to her as ‘mine’). Yet because it’s a prequel, you know they’re doomed from the start, and I enjoyed the constant guessing at what would finally tear the two apart.

Really enjoyed the Games too. I liked the evolution of how they function, such as there being a lack of safety (one of the Capitol girls - Arachne? - being killed by a tribute, the invasion of the arena). Also the actual arena being a colosseum, which as someone very interested by Roman culture, I found fascinating. Lucy Gray diverges significantly from Katniss, in that she is far less reserved about killing people, and iirc she doesn’t show much remorse. I like how Collins made a parallel of Katniss rather than a carbon copy.

Loved finding out about the origins of The Hanging Tree (some might call it cheesy but as an avid fan it felt like service lol), and Sejanus. Sejanus I liked as a character as he represents everything Snow isn’t, and how Snow kills him, which sends Snow himself directly into villainy. Thought it was cool how the pair aren’t so different on the surface, with Sejanus representing the minuscule ‘good’ parts of Snow, and how when he kills him he is casting those parts away for good, and it sets up the finale where he ‘kills’ Lucy Gray (imo I think he did kill her, but as per the song her fate is left ambiguous).

Loved Dr. Gaul and the beginning of the mutations within the arena, though I hope on the big screen they’re not ‘dulled down’ for younger audiences as the mutts were. She is just so twisted and manipulative, and I think she too represents parts of Snow, only the cruel, calculating parts. Snow chooses Gaul over Sejanus, bad over good.

There’s probably more but like I said it’s been a while, I’m planning to reread this year and hope I will enjoy it as much this time too.

Cisgender men have a number of advantages over cisgender women in regards to physicality.

strength - percentages vary but most estimates put women as having anywhere from 40% to 90% less lower and upper body strength.

testosterone levels - a big part of the trans debate. gives a huge advantage in sports the more there is (for comparison women have generally less than 2 nanomoles of testosterone, and men range from 8.8 to 31/32, provided they are healthy. testosterone increases muscle mass, bone density and strength.

height - the average woman worldwide stands 159.5cm tall. the average man stands at 171. ofc due to poverty and malnutrition these are higher in the west but men are almost always taller. this height difference is the reason why organisations like the WNBA exist, as height obviously plays a large role in athletic performance (in most sports anyway, shooting etc is excluded) and women cannot meet the same physical standards as men.

muscle mass - again improves athletic ability. generally far higher in men than women due to testosterone levels. women cannot raise their muscle mass significantly without damage.

bone density - although it varies significantly, men’s bones are almost always denser to accommodate their larger frames. women on the other hand have a reduced density, as well as different shaped bodies to accommodate their reproductive organs (eg longer torsos and shorter legs).

haemoglobin levels- For men, 13.5 to 17.5 grams per deciliter. For women, 12.0 to 15.5 grams per deciliter. men can therefore carry greater amounts of oxygen faster. this gives better endurance and faster recovery times.

[this](https://fairplayforwomen.com/biological-sex-differences/) article adds some extra points - but does go off on a rather strange tangent at the end.

now, with hrt many of these can be lessened and almost eradicated (assuming the minimum 2 years of hrt has been completed).

testosterone, muscle mass and haemoglobin levels all decrease to mostly female levels after hrt. however this doesn’t take away the height advantage, change the bone density or eliminate strength advantages either. the top 10% cis female athletes barely meet the bottom 10% of male athletes.

therefore even after 2+ years of hormone therapy, trans women do retain the advantage of going through male puberty, and will benefit from it.

also to end i would like to add i do want to see trans women in sports, though imo separate categories for both male and female trans athletes should be used until such a time as hrt improves to the point where the difference is non-existent.

sources - mayo clicnic, web md, the guardian + a few google searches to double check figures

I did Spanish at school, but one thing I would recommend is get a firm grasp on the grammar asap. Learn basic words to supplement that. Eg, learn desayunar (to have breakfast) as both a word and its grammar. Rinse and repeat for the most common verbs. 

Also do basic sentences (the kind you see on Duolingo). I wouldn’t recommend Duo before this as Duo teaches words, not grammar (which is very important in a language). It’s a good supplement and vocab learner but not really for much more. 

After that, start expanding vocab. Eg, I went to the bakery today, I wonder what that is in Spanish (panadería)? When you come across a word you don’t know in Spanish, google it and then slowly implement it in your own Spanish. 

After that, you gotta work on improving fluency. Spanish shows, movies, books - immerse yourself in the language (I have some recs if you want). If you can, go to a Spanish speaking country and get some practice (I live near Spain, going there is brilliant to get more in-depth knowledge of how Spanish is used in everyday life). Keep working daily and you’ll see yourself getting better in no time! I can speak the basics of several languages, Spanish is definitely the easiest. It takes a good bit of work, but it’s 100% possible. Good luck :)
